library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: postgres-socket-factory authenticates to one specific, real Cloud SQL instance via Google's SQL Admin API and mTLS certs issued for that instance; it cannot connect to an arbitrary local Postgres server, so the postgres:18-alpine container already used by org.postgresql:postgresql's own tests is not usable here, and there is no official Cloud SQL emulator or GCP-specific image in this repo's Docker allow-list. Follow the pattern already used by this repo's other GCP client-library tests (e.g. google-cloud-pubsub's test, which builds its client with NoCredentialsProvider.create() against a fake localhost:1 endpoint that nothing listens on, and google-cloud-firestore's test, which points FirestoreOptions at setEmulatorHost("localhost:8080") with no emulator actually running): register the driver via a JDBC URL like jdbc:postgresql:///<db>?cloudSqlInstance=<project>:<region>:<instance>&socketFactory=com.google.cloud.sql.postgres.SocketFactory with a syntactically valid but fake instance identifier and no real credentials, and assert on the expected failure (an IOException/SQLException from the failed Admin API lookup or auth step) rather than a successful connection. This still exercises credential-loading, HTTP client, and JSON-parsing code paths relevant to native-image reachability, consistent with how every other GCP client library in this repo is tested offline.
risks: Meaningful connection-level reachability coverage is inherently capped without live GCP credentials/instance; local Gradle and Native Image verification remain authoritative on how much of the library can actually be exercised.

jdbc-socket-factory-core (the transitive core) pulls in google-auth-library, google-api-client, google-api-services-sqladmin, and gax — overlapping surface with other already-supported Google client libraries in this repo, which may limit the marginal new coverage this library's own tests contribute.
